speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you've brought your husband in due to his bizarre and agitated behavior; let's start by having him tell me what exactly he has been experiencing lately and when it began. Has he had any recent physical illnesses, head injuries, or changes in his medication?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is concerning; he believes the NSA is controlling his mind and has been working on a device to stop it. Besides these delusions and the social withdrawal, has he experienced any hallucinations, such as hearing voices, or any physical symptoms like fever or headaches?

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, Folate, Urinalysis, Urine_Tox_Screen, CT_Head.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophrenia (first episode, paranoid type).

The normal lab results, including a negative toxicology screen and normal CT head, rule out substance use, metabolic causes, or structural brain lesions. Given the 6-week duration of bizarre delusions (paranoid persecution), the creation of a "mind-control" device, and the concurrent social withdrawal, the clinical picture is consistent with a primary psychotic disorder.
